MACD cross signals momentum shifts; filtering with RSI mid‑range (50‑60) prevents entry during extreme oscillations and ADX > 25 confirms a strong trend, while ATR‑based stops adapt to volatility, reducing risk of whipsaws and protecting profits in ranging markets.

A breakout beyond Bollinger bands signals a temporary trend shift; filtering it with an intermediate RSI range (50-70 for longs, 30-50 for shorts) captures momentum while avoiding extreme overbought/oversold noise, and ATR-based sizing limits exposure during high volatility periods, thereby reducing drawdown.

A price that breaks above the upper Bollinger band while RSI is in a bullish zone indicates a strong upward momentum; conversely a break below the lower band with a bearish RSI signals a downward move. Using ATR to set stop‑loss and take‑profit adapts the risk to current volatility, reducing false exits in choppy markets.
